title: B2+ · L11 — TED talk language analysis
description: Analizar y emular el lenguaje de TED talks: recursos retoricos, callbacks, tricolons, y estructura persuasiva.

questions.prompt: Preparas tu primer TED-x en TED-x. Necesitas los primeros 20 segundos que engancharan a la audiencia.
questions.question: Which TED-style hook is strongest?
options: Twenty years ago, I made a mistake that changed how I think about time.
questions.explanation: Formula magistral de hook TED: marco temporal especifico + historia personal + intriga + promesa de transformacion. Estudios de la propia TED muestran que los hooks con anecdota personal tienen 3x mas retention en los primeros 60 segundos que los que anuncian el tema. NUNCA empezar con 'Today I'll talk about' — es la firma del amateur. Registro: 'made a mistake that changed how I think' promete cambio, no informacion. Error hispano cultural: preferir 'introducir el tema' por politeness academica; en TED se rompe esa expectativa.
examples: Three years ago, I was told I had six months to live. → hook de vida-muerte
In 2011, I quit the best job I'd ever had. Everyone thought I was crazy. → hook de decision controvertida

questions.prompt: Estudias tecnicas retoricas para tu charla. El coach menciona 'tricolon'.
questions.question: What is a 'tricolon' in rhetoric?
options: A series of three parallel words or phrases for emphasis.
questions.explanation: Tricolon = agrupacion de tres elementos paralelos ('veni, vidi, vici' de Cesar; 'life, liberty, pursuit of happiness' de la Declaracion de Independencia; 'blood, sweat, and tears' de Churchill). El cerebro humano recuerda tres MUY bien: dos suena inacabado, cuatro suena a lista. Uso obligatorio en casi todo TED talk memorable. Regla practica: el tercer elemento suele ser el mas largo/climatico (rule of ascending tricolon). Registro: funciona en formal, informal, y politico universalmente.
examples: It's about people, planet, profit. → tricolon corporativo clasico
We came, we saw, we learned. → tricolon parafraseando Cesar (uso irónico moderno)

questions.statement: TED speakers deliberately use short, punchy sentences after long ones to create rhythm.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. La alternancia de longitud (largo/corto) es tecnica retorica central. La frase corta despues de una larga aterriza como martillo — cambio de velocidad que fuerza atencion. 'And that changed everything.' es cierre clasico tras setup largo. Fenomeno neurologico: monotono en longitud desactiva atencion; contraste la reactiva. Estudios de discurso de Aaron Sorkin (guionista de The West Wing) confirman uso deliberado del staccato tras la ola larga. Registro: aplica igual en TED, en editorial escrito, y en storytelling narrativo.
examples: For decades we assumed X, we invested in Y, we defended Z. We were wrong. → largo + corto rotundo
The data was clear, the case was strong, the moment was ripe. And still, nothing happened. → tension retorica

questions.prompt: Terminas tu charla y quieres cerrar el arco narrativo que abriste al inicio.
questions.question: Which is a classic TED-style 'callback'?
options: Referring back to the opening story at the closing to create emotional closure.
questions.explanation: Callback = referencia deliberada al opening durante el cierre para crear 'emotional closure'. Tecnica de standup comedy adoptada por TED: el cerebro humano ama los circulos narrativos cerrados. 'Twenty years ago I made that mistake — today, I make sure my daughter never does.' El callback activa satisfaccion neurologica y hace la charla memorable. Registro: obligatorio en cualquier keynote profesional; usado tambien en peliculas (setup/payoff). Error del amateur: cerrar con tesis nueva sin conectar al opening.
examples: Remember the mistake I mentioned at the start? Here's what it taught me. → callback explicito
That six-month diagnosis? I'm still here, twelve years later. → callback dramatico

questions.text: And here's the thing — the story we tell ourselves matters more than the facts themselves.
questions.explanation: 'And here's the thing' es signature phrase TED — anuncia que viene el insight central. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'here's the' con /zðə/ / dificil, tiende a asimilar /ˈhɪəzðə/; 'tell ourselves' con enlazado /telaʊə(r)selvz/; 'matters more' con /zm/ cluster /ˈmætəzmɔː/. Colocacion clave: 'the story we tell ourselves' es un frame retorico universal (adoptado desde psicologia narrativa) — inmensamente poderoso porque coloca al oyente como agente activo, no pasivo. Registro: TED puro.
examples: And here's the thing: nobody was going to save us. → cierre de setup con puntualizacion
But here's what I've learned — vulnerability is not weakness. → variante Brene Brown

questions.prompt: Estudias el discurso 'I have a dream' de MLK para tu propio TED.
questions.question: Which is an example of anaphora (repetition of opening words)?
options: I have a dream that... I have a dream that... I have a dream that...
questions.explanation: Anaphora = repeticion deliberada de la misma palabra o frase al INICIO de frases consecutivas. La usan MLK ('I have a dream'), Obama ('Yes we can'), Churchill ('We shall fight...'), casi todo cierre de convention politica. Crea ritmo hipnotico y anclaje emocional. Distinto de simple repeticion ('very very good' es enfatico banal, no anaphora). Anaphora inversa = epiphora (repetir al final). Registro: obligatoria en discursos elevados; puede rozar lo cursi si se abusa.
examples: We will not stop. We will not tire. We will not fail. → anaphora tricolon combinada
It's about who we are. It's about who we want to be. It's about our children. → anaphora emocional

questions.prompt: Empareja cada recurso retorico de TED con su traduccion:
questions.explanation: Cinco herramientas retoricas basicas del toolkit TED. Toda charla premiada las combina. Contrast pair ('not X, but Y') y CTA son estructurales (arquitectura de la charla); anecdota y metafora son emocionales (conexion afectiva). Rhetorical question funciona como puente reflexivo — invita al oyente a pensar sin exigirle responder. Registro: aplicables tambien a keynotes corporativos y presentaciones inversion (VCs esperan estas estructuras en pitch).
examples: Rhetorical: What if I told you happiness isn't a feeling? → invita reflexion
Contrast pair: It's not about working harder — it's about working differently. → estructura pivote

questions.target: We don't need more information. We need more courage to act on what we already know.
questions.explanation: Estructura magistral: contrast pair ('not X, but Y') + parallelism + climax accion. Frase memorable, tuiteable, quotable — cierra con verbo de accion ('act'). Este es el nivel 'idea worth spreading' condensada. Ritmo natural: primera oracion firme y descendente en 'information'; pausa marcada; segunda oracion con enfasis creciente en 'courage' y climax en 'know'. Contracciones: 'don't' obligatoria (no 'do not' que suena a legal document). Practica: graba y compara con tu tempo natural — probablemente vayas rapido, ralentiza.
examples: The problem isn't a lack of resources — it's a lack of resourcefulness. → wordplay potente
We don't rise to the level of our goals; we fall to the level of our systems. → James Clear paradigm

questions.prompt: Ultimos 30 segundos de tu TED. Quieres dejar a la audiencia pensando.
questions.question: Which TED closing style is most powerful?
options: So the next time you face this decision, ask yourself one question: [pause] what would you do if you weren't afraid?
questions.explanation: Cierre TED de referencia: (1) proyeccion al futuro del oyente ('next time you face this'), (2) pregunta poderosa con pausa marcada, (3) CTA implicito que dejaria al oyente pensando durante dias. 'Thank you for listening' es despues, ritualico y separado — el ULTIMO thought sustantivo debe ser la pregunta. 'What would you do if you weren't afraid?' es especificamente de Sheryl Sandberg — se ha convertido en formato prestado por miles de charlas. Registro: cierre = 30% del impacto total de la charla.
examples: So I'll leave you with this: what will you build? → pregunta abierta directa
The question isn't whether you can. It's whether you will. → contrast pair como cierre

questions.statement: Great TED talks avoid personal stories to stay universally relatable.
questions.explanation: FALSO — es al reverso. TODAS las TED talks top-rated (>10M vistas) incluyen historia personal especifica. Paradoja: mientras MAS especifica la anecdota, MAS universal la resonancia. Regla contraintuitiva del storytelling: 'the specific is the universal'. Brene Brown habla de su terapia; Andrew Solomon de su depresion; Simon Sinek del fracaso de su empresa. Sin anecdota personal la charla se percibe como articulo academico leido en voz alta. Error hispano academico: aspirar a 'objetividad universal' evitando la persona; TED premia la contraria.
examples: Every top-rated TED has a specific personal story (analisis de 500 charlas). → dato empirico
Universal truths land through particular experiences — that's the paradox of storytelling. → principio central

questions.prompt: Reescribes una frase floja usando 'rule of three'.
questions.question: Which sentence best uses 'rule of three'?
options: It was fast, it was loud, and it was completely unexpected.
questions.explanation: Rule of three con progresion ascendente: primeros dos elementos cortos ('fast', 'loud'), tercero mas largo y climatico ('completely unexpected'). Es rule of ASCENDING tricolon — el efecto de martillo climatico es 100x mas fuerte que tres elementos de igual longitud. Anaphora anadida ('it was...') refuerza el ritmo hipnotico. Registro: usable en storytelling, review de producto, discurso corporativo, incluso Instagram captions. Error tipico: hacer los tres elementos igual de largos — pierde el climax.
examples: It was raw, it was honest, and it changed the room. → ascending tricolon
She was smart, she was ruthless, and she never took no for an answer. → cerre climatico

questions.text: Imagine a world where every child, regardless of zip code, has access to the same quality of education.
questions.explanation: 'Imagine a world where...' es opening/pivot TED clasico — invita al oyente a visualizar (activa neuronas espejo). Fenomeno de connected speech: 'imagine a' con /nə/ /ɪˈmædʒɪnə/; 'regardless of' con weak form /rɪˈɡɑːdləsəv/; 'zip code' se dice como unidad /ˈzɪpkəʊd/. 'Zip code' es shorthand US para inequidad geografica (donde naces determina tu destino — poderoso porque asume que el oyente conoce esta metafora social americana). Registro: TED elevado, aspiracional.
examples: Imagine a world where healthcare followed you, not the other way around.
Picture this: a city where the air quality is measured street by street. → 'picture this' variante

questions.prompt: Analizas la ejecucion (delivery) de los TED speakers top. Que hacen distinto?
questions.question: Which is TRUE about TED speaker delivery?
options: They speak fast to fit more content.
They use strategic pauses to let ideas land.
questions.explanation: El SILENCIO es la herramienta mas subvalorada en public speaking. Pausar despues de una frase clave permite que el auditorio procese emocionalmente. Los amateurs corren (ansiedad); los pros pausan (confianza). Regla de Nancy Duarte: pausa deliberada de 2-3 segundos tras cada 'moneyshot line' (frase potente). Fenomeno psicologico: durante la pausa, el oyente COMPLETA la frase mentalmente — se convierte en co-creador del insight. Registro: el silencio requiere confianza; los principiantes lo temen.
examples: And then... [pause 2 sec] ...everything changed. → suspenso maximo
The answer is simple. [pause] But it's not easy. → contraste con pausa

questions.statement: 'One idea, well-told' is the guiding principle behind TED talks.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Chris Anderson (curador de TED) lo repite en cada TED speaker training: UNA idea, no cinco. La disciplina de elegir una y desarrollarla profundamente distingue talks memorables de olvidables. Regla practica: si no puedes resumir tu charla en UNA frase clara, cortala hasta que puedas. Charlas con 3-5 ideas se olvidan; charlas con 1 idea trascendente se citan por decadas. Registro: aplica igual a keynotes, essays, articulos de opinion. Error tipico academico: querer 'cubrir el tema' — matar la idea central.
examples: TED philosophy: If you can't summarize your talk in one sentence, cut. → regla operativa
One idea, deeply told, beats ten ideas shallowly listed. → principio central

questions.target: This isn't just a technology problem. It's a human problem. And it's on us to solve it.
questions.explanation: Cierre motivacional TED de referencia: tricolon (three punchy sentences) + escalation (technology → human → us) + accountability collective ('it's on us'). 'On us to solve' es lenguaje potente que llama a accion colectiva sin dedo acusador. Ritmo natural: tres frases con longitud ascendente, pausas breves entre ellas, tono creciente en enfasis. Contracciones: 'isn't', 'it's' obligatorias — 'is not' 'it is' rompen el ritmo staccato. Este template lo usan Simon Sinek, Susan Cain, Bill Gates en cierres emblematicos.
examples: This is not a policy issue. It's not a technical issue. It's a moral one. → escalation retorica
It's not their problem to fix — it's ours. And the time is now. → accountability + urgencia
